## Summary

Sueppel signals a new quantitative-finance working paper: *"Diversification Across Predictors: Heterogeneous Ensemble Learning for Cross-Sectional Return Prediction."* From the abstract:

- **Problem**: cross-sectional stock-return prediction — extremely low signal-to-noise, high-dimensional factor spaces, non-stationary predictor effectiveness. Failure modes are complementary: neural networks overfit noise (high variance) while linear models underfit nonlinear structure (high bias).
- **Proposal**: extend the financial principle of **diversification to the predictor level** — a bagging procedure combining linear and nonlinear predictors, so each model functions as a distinct specialist whose prediction errors exhibit **low cross-covariance**, enabling error cancellation upon aggregation.
- **Theory**: formalized via **bias-variance-covariance decomposition**, establishing an exact mathematical correspondence between portfolio diversification and predictor aggregation.
- **Results** (CSI300 daily-frequency **Alpha158** factor datasets): **Rank IC improvement >13%** over standalone neural networks; surpasses tree-based state-of-the-art methods (XGBoost, Double Ensemble) on both predictive-accuracy and portfolio-based evaluation metrics.

## Why it matters

- Second Sueppel-arXiv capture today ([[2026-11-19-sueppel-risvix-rough-squared-vix]]) — he is the vault's densest single macro/quant-research channel ([[2026-10-28-sueppel-regimerank-regime-aware-sector-ranking]]).
- The bias-variance-covariance framing is the transferable piece: "diversify across predictors the way you diversify across assets" gives a principled basis for running prediction threads as an equal-weighted committee of deliberately different specialists instead of picking a single winner model.
- Connects to the vault's ML-prediction verification thread: [[2026-11-18-quantbeckman-allocflow-reward-deploy-mismatch]] (train/deploy regime mismatch — this paper's "protection filter" stage is exactly the deployment-regime guard that thread demands) and [[2026-11-02-quantbeckman-kg-llm-sentiment-sharpe-skepticism]] (single-model ML claims).
- Skepticism gates: (1) working paper v1, Nov 2026 — no peer review, no replication; (2) single market (CSI300, China) and one factor set (Alpha158) — cross-sectional ensemble gains often shrink out-of-region; (3) ">13% Rank IC over standalone neural networks" partly measures how badly the standalone NN overfit, not absolute PnL quality — the paper claims portfolio metrics too, but the abstract gives no Sharpe/turnover numbers; (4) equal weighting + protection filter is deliberately simple — no transaction-cost or turnover treatment visible in the abstract.

Task filed: pull the full paper, verify the >13% Rank IC claim and the XGBoost/Double-Ensemble comparison, and judge whether "diversify across predictors" is worth adopting as a desk principle.
